title: review_ledger
description: The approval ledger: every human review verdict recorded against the corpus, one entry per (record, field, locale), anchored to the sha256 of the exact text the reviewer read. HAND-AUTHORED. It is not measured from the data and build_schemas.py will never write it, because an empty ledger is the correct starting state and a generator pointed at zero entries would narrow the contract to {}. The addressing rules and the decision behind them are in design/review_ledger.md (APP_PLAN D4); the reader/writer is scripts/review_ledger.py.

note.description: What this file is, for whoever opens it first. Internal prose, never learner-facing.

entries.description: The verdicts. An empty array is VALID and is the state before any teacher has signed anything off — the ledger's job is to make the difference between 'nobody has reviewed this' and 'somebody reviewed it once' checkable, and it can only do that by existing while still empty.

Entry.description: One verdict. It addresses (slug, field, locale) and anchors to content_hash. There is NO expiry field and there will not be one: an approval is invalidated by a rewrite, not by the calendar (D4). A rewrite makes the entry STALE — it stops being exported and is reported — and staleness is computed, never stored.

slug.description: The published address of the record reviewed. The integer `id` some registries carry is a storage row number and must never appear here.

entity.description: Optional. The entity the slug belongs to, as contracts/manifest.json names it. Redundant with the slug's namespace and kept only so a hand-written entry can say what it means; when present it must agree with the record actually found.

field.description: The reviewed field, or "*" for the whole record. A field-level entry is what makes an approval survivable: a campaign that rewrites `translation` invalidates exactly that approval and leaves the `structure_explanation` sign-off standing. `dissection` is a virtual field — the per-token glosses reviewed as one artefact, exactly as scripts/review_queue.py presents them.

locale.description: The locale reviewed. Absent (or "*") means locale-agnostic — correct for a mechanical field, wrong for prose: approving a pt-BR translation must not bless the `en` anchor beside it, which is why D4 makes the locale part of the address.

content_hash.description: sha256 (NFC-normalised) of the exact value the reviewer read, as scripts/review_queue.py computes it: sha(text) for one locale of a locale-object, sha_json(value) for an aggregate, and the record hash minus its own review_status stamp for field "*". A truncated prefix of at least 8 hex characters joins a full digest, so a ledger written from the queue's 24-character short hash and a hash recomputed from the export still meet. An entry with no anchor is refused, not tolerated.

status.description: The verdict. Two values, because a ledger with six spellings of "yes" is a ledger nobody can audit; scripts/review_queue.py accepts a wider historical set on READ and this is what we WRITE. Vocabulary owner: design — design/review_ledger.md. Widening it is an edit there, never a side effect of regenerating this schema from the data.

reviewed_by.description: Who reviewed it. Required: an anonymous approval is not a review, and the correction-rate metric (W39) is per reviewer. A stable handle, not a mailbox — no PII beyond what the owner chooses to record.

approved_at.description: When. Kept for provenance and ordering, NOT for expiry — nothing reads this to decide whether an approval still holds.

note.description: Optional internal note from the reviewer. Not learner-facing and never exported into a record.

x-yomineko.generated_by: HAND-AUTHORED — build_schemas.py lists it in LEDGER (part of HANDWRITTEN) and must never write it.
x-yomineko.vocabulary_policy: Every value set here is design-owned and carries x-vocabulary naming design/review_ledger.md. Nothing in this file was measured, because there is nothing to measure until a teacher starts working.
